attempt.learner: model-learner (reference attempt authored with the case)

commit.management: Intravenous calcium gluconate under cardiac monitoring with oral calcium and calcitriol alongside, serial calciums until stability, endocrine and operating-surgeon follow-up -- executing the calcium-replacement protocol the index operation's dp6 decision chose (trace 30); discharge when symptoms have resolved and calcium is stable or rising on the oral regimen, with the transient-versus-permanent question carried to follow-up (the ATA statement's 6-month line, C52). The commit is right; the debrief's scored error is the stage it was reached at, not the destination.

debrief_text.reactions: PEARLS reactions: a strong, instructive performance with one scored anchoring event, and its most interesting feature is where the anchor lived. The learner did not invent the anxiety frame -- she inherited it from the ward note, held it as her lead hypothesis at stage 1 (0.34 against the truth's 0.30), and was still holding it at 0.26 at stage 2, after her own hands had elicited Trousseau's sign and the workbench had retired the hypothesis across the rule-out line. What released her was not a new fact about the patient but the panel: the first evidence in the case that the frame could not absorb. Her stage-4 board (truth 0.86, Brier 0.0244) is the best-calibrated close in the module's recent cases; the cost of the anchor was a stage, not the diagnosis.
debrief_text.description: Stage 1: the learner leads with the inherited frame -- anxiety/hyperventilation 0.34, the truth 0.30, neck hematoma 0.10 (the airway question properly priced) -- and orders only the bedside battery. What she does NOT do is the case's stage-1 story: the calcium panel, available from stage 1 and already chosen in embryo by the operation's dp6 protocol, is not ordered, although a corrected calcium of 7.8 mg/dL sits in the chart from the day before, filed under the very frame she has adopted. Her Brier is 0.6384 against the workbench's 0.4144 -- the workbench, which weights the trace-30 debrief as evidence, already leads with the truth at 0.42. Stage 2: Trousseau's sign is positive on her own examination; the workbench moves the truth to 0.9445 and retires all five rivals; she moves the truth only to 0.52 and keeps the frame at 0.26 -- the anchoring event (stage 2, hyp.anxiety-hyperventilation), the fifth installation shape in this module's series: premature closure on a benign attribution, installed by inheritance before the case began and surviving evidence she personally elicited. To her credit, her stage-2 orders are exactly right -- ECG and the calcium panel. Stage 3: the panel returns the conjunction (corrected 7.3 and falling, ionized 0.94, PTH 8, phosphate high, magnesium normal, pH normal) and the tier block classifies iv-calcium-indicated; she releases the frame to 0.06 and moves the truth to 0.78 (Brier 0.0598). Her ECG classifies non-contributory -- ordered for the QT (486 ms, the tracing the monitored infusion needed), and the case records that verdict as the classification's limit, not the order's. Stage 4: commit hyp.postop-hypoparathyroidism at 0.86, Brier 0.0244, with the intravenous-tier management the block computed. Total resource tally: 50 minutes, 5 units.
debrief_text.analysis: The anchor's mechanics are the fifth shape in this module's series. Case 4's was installed by another clinician, case 5's by the learner's own true history, case 6's by a test result, case 7's by social pressure. This one is premature closure by inheritance: a benign, mechanistically real explanation (hyperventilation genuinely produces these symptoms, C61) was attached to the symptoms by the ward note before the case began, and its plausibility did the work that evidence usually has to do -- it absorbed the day-1 calcium (a value below the ATA line, filed unactioned), it shaped the learner's stage-1 board, it survived the Trousseau sign she elicited herself, and it set her stage-1 orders: the cheap bedside test the frame was comfortable with, not the panel the protocol had already pointed at. Three features distinguish this shape. First, the discriminating evidence PREDATED the encounter: unlike case 6's BNP or case 7's pressured CTPA, nothing new had to arrive to break the frame -- the debrief and the day-1 value were both in the record from the start, and the failure was one of reading, not of information. Second, the mimic is honest: hyperventilation alkalosis really does lower ionized calcium and produce perioral tingling and tetany (C61), which is why the frame feels like physiology rather than bias -- the discriminating tests are therefore not 'is she anxious?' (she is, and irrelevantly) but the total calcium, the PTH, and the pH, the three legs the mimic cannot produce. Third, the release came from the learner's own orders: she bought the panel at stage 2 despite the frame, and the frame did not survive its return. The lesson the case is built to teach is not 'distrust anxiety' -- it is that an attribution in the record is a hypothesis with an author, and it must re-earn its place against the chart's own numbers like any other.
debrief_text.summary: Postoperative hypoparathyroidism declaring as symptomatic hypocalcemia on days 1-2 after a total thyroidectomy whose own debrief had computed it. The learner inherited the record's anxiety frame, anchored on it through her own positive Trousseau sign (one scored event, the module's fifth shape), ordered the right tests a stage late, and committed the truth at 0.86 with the intravenous-tier management the block computed -- executing, in the end, the calcium-replacement protocol the operation had chosen two days earlier. Formative only; the expert-review gate remains UNMET.
